summary: Markets posted modest gains Friday as SK Hynix made a spectacular U.S. debut, raising $26.5 billion in the largest foreign IPO ever and surging 13% on day one. The S&P 500 rose 0.42% to 7,575.39 while the Nasdaq added 0.29%, capping a positive week despite renewed Middle East tensions. Meta Platforms extended its rally, gaining 6% Friday and notching a 15% weekly gain after AI chip production announcements. Geopolitical risks simmered as Trump declared the Iran ceasefire 'over,' though oil retreated as talks continued. Crypto markets held above key support levels—Bitcoin near $64,000 and Ethereum around $1,795—despite $95 million in BTC ETF outflows Thursday. Looking ahead, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is set to testify before Congress on Monday alongside key CPI data, with the next FOMC meeting scheduled for July 28-29. Markets remain on hold awaiting Q2 earnings season, which kicks off next week with major financials including JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Goldman Sachs.

signals.title: SK Hynix smashes IPO records with $26.5B raise, shares jump 13% on debut
signals.desc: South Korean chipmaker's blockbuster listing signals strong institutional appetite for AI-exposed semiconductor plays, lifting broader tech sentiment despite memory chip competition concerns.

signals.title: Meta surges 15% weekly on AI chip production plans, strengthening tech leadership
signals.desc: Reuters report that Meta will begin producing proprietary AI chips in September drove sustained buying, with the stock posting its best weekly performance since early 2024.

signals.title: Bitcoin holds $64,000 despite $95M ETF outflows as institutional rotation continues
signals.desc: Second consecutive day of ETF outflows failed to break key technical support, though rotation from BlackRock's IBIT into Fidelity's FBTC suggests cautious positioning rather than capitulation.

signals.title: Ethereum ETFs post $52M outflows amid weak onchain activity and rising leverage
signals.desc: ETH dropped below $1,800 as derivative leverage expanded faster than meaningful network activity, with median transaction values down 77% week-over-week despite 40% volume increase.

signals.title: Fed Chair Warsh testimony and June CPI loom as July FOMC holds steady at 3.5-3.75%
signals.desc: Markets price in 75% odds of no rate change at July 28-29 meeting, but next week's CPI print and congressional testimony could shift September expectations if inflation remains sticky above 3%.

verdict: Markets consolidate near highs ahead of earnings deluge and critical CPI data, with tech leadership intact but crypto flows turning cautious.
